title: Composite action expands caller-supplied with: inputs into shell script text
description: action.yml is published as a composite action that third-party workflows run (`uses: memeshee/zanary@main` is the documented whole setup: action.yml:7, docs/CI.md:49). Its five inputs (flow, expect, anchor, ttl-days, out; action.yml:23-46) are free-form strings with no validation, and the action places their `${{ inputs.* }}` values in the script text of its `run:` steps -- the gate step (:95, :100, :103, :106, :116, :117), the always-run job summary step (:140) and the verdict step (:177-178) -- instead of receiving them through env: or argv. The runner substitutes those expressions into the script before bash parses it, so a value carrying shell syntax (a quote plus ;, $( ), backticks, #) is executed by the calling job's shell. The gate step also writes the value derived from inputs.out into GITHUB_OUTPUT as one raw, unescaped line (:107), so the value leaves the step as a step output and is re-interpolated into script text at :136 (job summary, `if: always()`) and :153 (rig diagnostics); the verdict step interpolates the step's exit_code output the same way (:175, numeric in this action's flow). Nothing in this repository triggers it: the documented consumer setup passes literal values (docs/CI.md:49-55, the flow literal at :51) and this repository's own gate passes static matrix entries defined in the same file (.github/workflows/privacy-gate.yml:87-93 from the matrix at :71-80). The defect is in the action as a library: it hands every consumer that templates one of the five inputs into `with:` a code-execution sink in that consumer's own job.
root_cause: The action treats caller-supplied input values as script fragments rather than data. `${{ inputs.* }}` values are placed in `run:` script text at eight sites (:95, :100, :103, :106, :116, :117, :140, :177-178, counting the two verdict lines as one site), and no value is passed through env: or argv anywhere in the file (action.yml has no env: block at all). Nothing validates or rejects shell syntax, so the double quotes around the substitutions are the sole barrier and $( ) / backticks defeat them. Values derived from the inputs are then written to GITHUB_OUTPUT on one raw, unescaped line (:107), which both lets them leave the step as a step output and re-enter script text in later steps (:136, :153); the exit_code output is interpolated the same way at :175.
intended_behavior: with: inputs are data, not code: each step should take them through env: (or argv) so a value cannot change which commands run; out should be written to GITHUB_OUTPUT with the multiline-safe key<<DELIM form; and steps.gate.outputs.*, which are derived from the inputs, must be passed the same way instead of being re-inserted into script text.

trace.description: The action accepts five caller-supplied strings (flow, expect, anchor, ttl-days, out; lines 23-46) with no format validation; a third-party workflow supplies them in its own repository via with:.

trace.scope: step run the gate - run: script text
trace.description: The runner substitutes ${{ inputs.flow }} into the script text (a double-quoted assignment) before bash parses it; the identical pattern sits at lines 100, 103, 106, 116, 117 and in the job summary / verdict steps (140, 177-178). Reproduced locally: with a payload in flow the injection executed here, and also at :100 when the value was invalid.

trace.scope: step run the gate - step output write
trace.description: The out value is appended raw to GITHUB_OUTPUT (no key/newline escaping), so it also leaves the step as a step output and re-enters later scripts at 136, 153 and 175. Reproduced locally: the recorded value kept its $( ) text verbatim and executed again when the job summary step was rendered with it.

trace.scope: step run the gate - command context
trace.description: OUT is assigned from ${{ github.workspace }} and ${{ inputs.out }}, so the expansion lands in a double-quoted assignment in command position: a value with $( ), backticks, a closing quote plus ;, or # is executed by the caller shell (independently reproduced on this line and on line 95 with marker payloads in the offline sandbox).

evidence.description: FLOW is assigned from ${{ inputs.flow }} inside the run the gate step - flow is expanded into script text.
second expansion of flow in the same step (the no-flow-definition error path) - a payload runs here as well (reproduced: two executions for one invalid value).
OUT is assigned from ${{ github.workspace }} and ${{ inputs.out }} - out expanded into a command context (the verified local run B).
the anchor input is expanded into script text in the [ anchor = true ] test.
expect is expanded inside the probe command line (--expect argument).
ttl-days is expanded the same way (--ttl-days argument).

the echo of out=$OUT into $GITHUB_OUTPUT - raw write, no newline escaping; the value leaves the step as a step output and a newline in it can forge further output lines (reproduced: an injected payload=owned key).
OUT is assigned from ${{ steps.gate.outputs.out }} in the always-run job summary step - the stored value re-enters script text (same at 153 in rig diagnostics); verified by execution.
code is assigned from ${{ steps.gate.outputs.exit_code }} in the verdict step - the output that decides the build result is also script text (numeric in this action's flow).
the title argument of the job summary step expands inputs.flow and inputs.expect; that step runs with if: always().
inputs.expect is expanded inside the verdict step case branches (also line 178).
the documented consumer setup passes literal values (flow: flows/my-checkout.json), which is why no in-repo caller triggers the injection.

conditions.description: A calling workflow passes a non-constant value (a reusable-workflow parameter, a dispatch or matrix value, or an event-derived string) to one of flow, expect, anchor, ttl-days, out. No caller in this repository does that: the documented setup passes literals (docs/CI.md:49-55) and .github/workflows/privacy-gate.yml:87-93 passes static matrix entries defined in the same file at :71-80, so nothing fires here.

execution.attacker_perspective: Whoever controls a value that a consumer workflow passes into the action inputs -- a contributor-influenced branch/PR-derived string, a reusable-workflow parameter, a dispatch input, or the consumer's own templated value -- gets the calling job's shell: the payload runs in the action's steps with that job environment (GITHUB_* variables, the step outputs, any job/step environment the step can see). A consumer that passes a literal cannot be attacked; the defect is that the action makes the templating pattern dangerous.
instructions: Read action.yml from the read-only target (commit 7058406, worktree clean) and assert the verbatim text of every interpolation site: :95, :96, :100, :103, :106, :107, :116, :117, :136, :140, :153, :175, :177, :178.

Render the gate step's run-block (verbatim lines 92-129) with the literal expression substitution the Actions runner documents (plus ${{ github.workspace }} and ${{ github.action_path }}), one payload value per run: flow kept valid, flow made invalid (so :100 expands it again), out, and out with a newline; all other inputs benign literals.

Run each rendered script with `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail` inside `docker run --rm --network=none --cpus=6 --memory=3500m --pids-limit=1024 --user 1000:1000 -v <disposable copy>:/t -w /t/verifier10/action rust:1-slim`, with GITHUB_OUTPUT / GITHUB_WORKSPACE / GITHUB_ACTION_PATH / GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY set and a placeholder ./target/release/zanary-probe (the real rig is out of bounds); each payload only appends one byte to a counter file so the execution count is visible.
Clear the counters and the output file first, and run a control pass with every input a literal.

Then render the always-run job summary step (action.yml:136-147) with the exact out= value the gate step recorded in GITHUB_OUTPUT and execute it the same way (the step-output round trip), with a benign-value render as the control; stop at the first observed boundary result.
execution.observed_result: Independently reproduced in the offline sandbox with command-substitution payloads (no quote-breaking needed) against the verbatim gate run-block, rendered with literal expression substitution as the runner documents it and with a placeholder probe. Control (all inputs literal): the step ran normally, wrote out=/t/verifier10/ws/z and exit_code=0, and no counter file appeared. Flow payload (valid value): executed at :95 (counter x) while the step still finished normally, exit 0, with its own outputs. Flow payload (invalid value): executed twice (counter xx), at :95 and in the :100 error echo, then exited 2. Out payload: executed at :103 (counter x) and the step exited 0 having written the raw value out=/t/verifier10/ws/x$(printf y >> /t/verifier10/count-roundtrip.txt) and exit_code=0 to GITHUB_OUTPUT. Rendering the always-run job summary step with that recorded value executed the embedded fragment at :136 (counter y), while the benign-value control executed nothing. A newline in the out value made GITHUB_OUTPUT contain out=/t/verifier10/ws/x, payload=owned and exit_code=0, i.e. an injected output key. Nothing outside the disposable copy was written; --network=none, placeholder probe, no rig and no live runner. The only element not executed here is the runner's own substitution step (documented behavior; a live runner is out of bounds).

remediation.strategy: Keep inputs as data on both sides of every step: declare them under env: and reference the environment variables inside the scripts; validate the shapes the action actually needs (flow/out caller-workspace-relative paths; expect in {pass, fail}; anchor in {true, false}; ttl-days a positive integer) and fail early with a clear error; keep the existing three-candidate flow search operating on the env value; write out to GITHUB_OUTPUT with the multiline-safe key<<DELIM form; and in the job summary, rig diagnostics and verdict steps pass steps.gate.outputs.out / steps.gate.outputs.exit_code through env: instead of re-interpolating them.

code_changes.fixed_code:
- name: run the gate
      id: gate
      shell: bash
      working-directory: ${{ github.action_path }}
      env:                                    # every input arrives as data
        INPUT_FLOW: ${{ inputs.flow }}
        INPUT_OUT: ${{ inputs.out }}
        INPUT_EXPECT: ${{ inputs.expect }}
        INPUT_ANCHOR: ${{ inputs.anchor }}
        INPUT_TTL_DAYS: ${{ inputs.ttl-days }}
      run: |
        set -o pipefail
        case "$INPUT_EXPECT" in pass|fail) ;; *) echo "::error::expect must be pass or fail"; exit 2 ;; esac
        case "$INPUT_TTL_DAYS" in ''|*[!0-9]*) echo "::error::ttl-days must be a positive integer"; exit 2 ;; esac
        FLOW="$INPUT_FLOW"
        for candidate in "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$FLOW" "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/$FLOW" "$FLOW"; do
          if [ -f "$candidate" ]; then FLOW="$candidate"; break; fi
        done
        if [ ! -f "$FLOW" ]; then echo "::error::ZANARY gate: no flow definition at $INPUT_FLOW"; exit 2; fi
        OUT="$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/$INPUT_OUT"; mkdir -p "$OUT"
        anchor_flag=""
        if [ "$INPUT_ANCHOR" = "true" ]; then anchor_flag="--anchor"; fi
        { echo "out<<ZANARY_OUT"; printf '%s\n' "$OUT"; echo "ZANARY_OUT"; } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        set +e
        timeout "${ZANARY_GATE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-2700}" ./target/release/zanary-probe test \
          --definition "$FLOW" --out "$OUT" --expect "$INPUT_EXPECT" \
          --ttl-days "$INPUT_TTL_DAYS" $anchor_flag --summary "$OUT/test.json" 2>&1 | tee "$OUT/gate.log"
        code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
        if [ "$code" = "124" ]; then
          echo "::warning::the gate did not finish within ${ZANARY_GATE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-2700}s - treating it as a rig failure"
          code=2
        fi
        echo "exit_code=$code" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
        exit 0
    # Later steps (job summary, rig diagnostics, verdict) take GATE_OUT / GATE_EXIT
    # through env: (env: GATE_OUT: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.out }}) and never
    # re-interpolate ${{ }} inside script text.

likelihood.reason: No caller in this repository passes a non-constant value (docs/CI.md:49-55 and privacy-gate.yml:87-93 both pass constants), so exploitation requires a consumer that templates one of the five inputs from a reusable-workflow parameter, a dispatch input, a branch/PR-derived string or similar -- a caller-side pattern the defect makes dangerous but cannot guarantee.

impact.reason: When it fires, arbitrary commands run inside the consumer's CI job as the runner user: the action's own steps, their step outputs (including the value the later steps trust) and any job or step environment the step can see. No in-repo caller is templated, so the impact lands on consumers of memeshee/zanary@main rather than on this repository's own CI.

confidence.reason: Every interpolation site, the raw GITHUB_OUTPUT write and the step-output round trip were re-read line-by-line at commit 7058406 (worktree clean; action.yml sha256 1c58ef4994e322ff0b222943132de8744dbdb35f6af59c842c595f8db43acde3 -- the hunter's recorded 6e58f6bb... is the same content without its trailing newline), and the expansion was re-executed independently in the offline sandbox with my own command-substitution payloads (flow at :95 and :100, out at :103, and the recorded value executing again at :136) against a benign-value control that ran nothing. The only step not executed here is the runner's own expression substitution (documented behavior, and a live runner is out of bounds for this run), and exploitation still requires a consumer that templates a value into with:, which the low likelihood records.
